<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7053333e1e2194cea2e21d8b2e1c9b6f081fcfa6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d5dcc10a9e972aaeb43a8377400cd597d9d9d04` — the merge of head `64f47976620529c3d3938a3240eab5233c10e248` into base `7053333e1e2194cea2e21d8b2e1c9b6f081fcfa6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d5dcc10a9e972aaeb43a8377400cd597d9d9d04 && git checkout 1d5dcc10a9e972aaeb43a8377400cd597d9d9d04
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7053333e1e2194cea2e21d8b2e1c9b6f081fcfa6 64f47976620529c3d3938a3240eab5233c10e248 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7053333e1e2194cea2e21d8b2e1c9b6f081fcfa6 && git merge --no-ff 64f47976620529c3d3938a3240eab5233c10e248

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7053333e1e2194cea2e21d8b2e1c9b6f081fcfa6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64f47976620529c3d3938a3240eab5233c10e248`
Local-runs: none

Head re-read twice this act and unmoved. Inputs, and nothing else: card #20731 (body; triage 5901376430; claim 5903072480; os-dev-report 5903655620), PR #20770 (body, its 7-file list, the net diff against `main` from the merge-base `a51920f5fb`), PR #20728 as precedent (merged as `1940afdaf`), and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-09-30T04:40Z: 35 in all; 32 completed `success`, 3 completed `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 0 in progress, 0 failed. Green includes Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check (the spec artifact gates inside it: api-surface, authorable-surface), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Test Core 1 to 6, the Dogfood gates, Spec property liveness.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set: unchanged — right.** No Zod schema, authorable key, conversion or migration registry is in the diff; `check:authorable-surface` and Spec property liveness are green.

**Public surface, `@objectstack/spec` (`/system`, `export * from './i18n-resolver'`).**
- `translateView(view, bundle, opts?)`: the third parameter widens from `ResolveOptions` to `TranslateDocumentOptions` — right. That type already existed and was exported (`extends ResolveOptions`, adds only `packagedBase?: unknown`; `translateObject` and `translateDashboard` take it). A `ResolveOptions` value is assignable to it, so every existing call compiles unchanged; on `main` the dispatcher table `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS` was already typed on `TranslateDocumentOptions`, so the base was handed to `translateView` and ignored — the PR body's reading of the cause is true. `check:api-surface` records export names plus `defineX` factory signature hashes only, so this widening is not caught mechanically; the changeset carries it, correctly.
- No export added, removed or renamed — right. `packagedDashboardPart` to `packagedPart` is a private rename; `valueOverridesPackagedBase` stays private; `scalarOverridesPackagedBase`'s exported signature is untouched.
- Behaviour with no base: `asRecord(undefined | null)` is `undefined`; `valueOverridesPackagedBase(undefined, …)` is `false` for every string and `packagedPart(undefined, …)` is `undefined`, so every branch takes the pre-change call with the same arguments and the return statement is not in the diff. "Without `packagedBase` the output is byte-identical to before" — true.
- Behaviour with a base: the comparison is the ONE function PR #20728 introduced (`valueOverridesPackagedBase`, the body behind `scalarOverridesPackagedBase`), and its three conservative edges are kept (no base → false; non-string or empty value → false; exact equality). No second comparison — right, as triage ordered. Coverage per string (view `label` and `description`; each def's `label`, `confirmText`, `confirmLabel`; each param's `label`, `help`, `placeholder`, matched by `name`; a def or param the base lacks answers `{}` and counts as authored) mirrors `translateDashboard`'s "a part the base does not carry" rule — right. An inline locale-map label is never an override; an edit back to the shipped string is a no-op — pinned.
- `translateDashboard`: only the finder's name changes at its four call sites, same keys, same body — unchanged, right.

**Public surface, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.**
- `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getPackagedViewBase(name): unknown` — one new public method, additive; like `getPackagedDashboardBase` it sits on no interface — right.
- `getPackagedDashboardBase` now delegates to the private `packagedArtifactBase('dashboard', name)`, whose body is the former method's body line for line (non-string or empty guard, `lookupArtifactItem`, catch to `undefined`). "Answers exactly as before" — true. `lookupArtifactItem` prefers `registry.getArtifactItem` (composite package-qualified entries first) and, on the `getItem` fallback, drops an item without a genuine `_packageId`, so an overlay hydrated under the plain key is never the base — the shadow-immunity claim is true.
- The key: the base is matched by the served view's registry identity, the qualified `OBJECT.VIEW_KEY`. `expandViewContainer` composes `name` as object plus dot plus key; the objectql boot (`engine.ts`, the `views` arm) registers each expanded item under that name with the owner package id and keeps the container under the bare object key; `viewTranslationKey` strips the prefix for the catalog. The bare key is not an identity (the showcase `zh-CN` bundle carries `_views.in_progress` under two objects). Stated in the body and TSDoc, pinned in `protocol-packaged-view-base.test.ts` (the KEY test: two objects, and the bare key answers `undefined`) and in `i18n-resolver.test.ts` (composes the identity). Triage's "states which key the base is matched by, and pins it" — met.
- No served answer changes with this PR — true. `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` `packagedObjectBaseOf` answers `undefined` for every type but `object` (the item read gates on `metaType === 'object'` before calling it); `rest-server.ts` translates `object` only; `getPackagedViewBase` has no reader outside the two test files. The `/meta` view arm is left to #20730's per-type resolver; this diff adds no resolver — "not a second resolver" respected.

**Ledger.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains one row (`protocol-packaged-view-base.test.ts`, `findOne`, pinned 1), the twin of the dashboard test's row; the double calls `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` — right.

**Shipped prose, sentence by sentence.**
- Both changesets: every factual sentence is true against the code, including "Every existing call compiles unchanged", "`translateMetadataDocument` already passed it through", "No serving layer in this release passes a view base yet", "No existing read changes answer, and `getPackagedDashboardBase` answers exactly as before", "Nothing is removed or renamed". One simplification: the protocol changeset says the bare key "answers `undefined`" flatly; the TSDoc carries the exact condition (unless some package registers a view under that literal name). Acceptable as CHANGELOG text.
- New and edited TSDoc: true. The measured reading it cites (`In Progress (edited-20680)`, `进行中`, admin or member, item or list) is the card's own; ADR-0126's regime table lists `view` under O (overlay), which supports "a packaged view is overlay-editable"; ADR-0029 D9.2a and its "same comparison, one layer down" requirement are quoted as the resolver already records them.
- PR body (the squash message): true throughout — the line references to `main` (`i18n-resolver.ts:906`, `:1407`, `protocol.ts:7194`), H1 to H4, the reader list, the published-surface section, the 12 and 10 pin counts, the commit lineage (`a3f753cead` then `64f4797662`) — with ONE FALSE SENTENCE: "The CLI's `i18n-bulk-action-coverage` test drives `translateView` without a base and is green (17 of 17)". `packages/cli/test/i18n-bulk-action-coverage.test.ts` imports `collectExpectedEntries`, `extractTranslations`, `computeI18nCoverage` and `ObjectTranslationDataSchema`; it names `translateView` in comments only and never calls it. The no-base readers that ARE green are the pre-existing spec blocks (`translateView — bulkActionDefs (#14253)`, the `translateMetadataDocument('view', …)` tests) and the REST read gate, all under Test Core. Wrong witness, right conclusion; not a contract fact. Ask of the adopting seat: remove or correct that sentence in the PR body before the squash — a body edit moves no head, so this record stands.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/20731-spec-view-catalog-override.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `minor` — right. A parameter widened to an extension of its former type is additive; a fix that also widens a published signature takes `minor`, not `patch` (Post-Task Checklist 3: a `yes` declaration takes at least `minor`).
- `.changeset/20731-metadata-protocol-packaged-view-base.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor` — right. One new public method, nothing removed. Both packages are released (17.5.0, neither private), so `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- Neither change is breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker and no migration is owed; `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:adr-0087-registration` and Check Changeset are green.
- The PR body declares Clause ② as `yes` — right: the diff widens the public surface (one exported function's parameter type, one new protocol method) while the accept-set is unchanged. No `(widening)` or `(narrowing)` arm is written, which the closed pair permits; `(narrowing)` would have been false. Both `minor` levels are consistent with the declaration, and with the dispatch's order.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from the os-dev-report deviations and the PR body:
1. The rule also covers the bulk-action copy, measured on the label only — answered, accepted. The rule belongs to the translator (the dashboard twin covered every string it translates); leaving the defs out would let an edited view label win while an edited def label on the same document loses. Pinned per string in the new spec block, including a tenant-added def and param. "Not measured on a running app" is declared in the body; the `/meta` view arm's verification is its carrier.
2. The refactor inside the surface (`packagedPart`; the private `packagedArtifactBase`) — answered, accepted. Both private; the dashboard call sites and the accessor body are unchanged; the dashboard pins ride in Test Core (green). H1's corrected premise (the comparison was already one function) is true.
3. `Part of #20731`, not `Fixes` — answered, right. Nothing served changes until the `/meta` view arm; the Part-of check is green; the card stays open. Escalated to the adopting seat, not to the dev: at landing, file the `/meta` view arm as the per-layer child on #20730's per-type resolver, or fold it into #20730's PR, "whichever the seats agree" (triage 5901376430). A seat act, not a review blocker.
4. Reproduced at the translator and protocol layer, not in a real `/meta` boot — answered, accepted. Triage placed the pins "at the translator and protocol layer"; the real-boot reach is the card's own (#20680 probe3); H4 was measured at RestServer's real route handlers with a protocol double, which is where the dormancy claim is decided.
5. `origin/main` merged once at `a51920f5fb`, commits since — answered. Read now: `main` has taken 6 commits since the merge-base (`cba417a8f2` through `eead9dcf40`); none touches any of the PR's 7 files; `c9c182ed14` touches `packages/spec` (`migrations/registry.ts` and an unrelated ui test), so the body's "none of them touches these packages" was true at PR-open and is now stale in wording only. An in-memory `git merge-tree` of the head onto current `main` is conflict-free; the queue rebuilds on current `main`.
6. The three out-of-scope notes — answered, each consistent with triage: (a) the `/meta` view arm rides #20730's per-type resolver as one more arm, and the open card is its tracker, so no new filing is owed; (b) the `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` view sentence is deferred by triage until the rule is observable, next to #20730's dashboard sentence; (c) the console's client-side re-resolution of `_views` labels is unmeasured and declared, its carrier the `/meta` arm's browser verification. Noted, not filed — right under Prime Directive 10: no new reproducible defect beyond the open card.
7. (report only) `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test -- --maxWorkers=2` may have dropped its flag — irrelevant to the contract; the head's Test Core shards are the gate.
8. (report only) the three authored commits carry the model-free trailer pair; the merge commit `a3f753cead` carries none. Squash is the repository's only merge method (title from the PR title, message from the PR body); the PR title and body carry no model identifier (scanned), so nothing from a branch commit message lands.
